subject: Output entitlement matrix & legal runbook
messages:
From: Cassandra Liu <cassandra@novum.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>
Cc: Mike Turner <mike.turner@novum.ai>, Novum Legal <contracts@novum.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Output entitlements & training — order form follow-up

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal asked me to follow up on two narrow but high-impact points in the order form / MSA before we can route for signature:

1) Output ownership: we need clearer language about whether Novum gets an assignment or an exclusive license to outputs generated by models hosted under the contract.
2) Training & feedback: Novum's security team is asking for an explicit opt-out for model retraining with customer-provided data and a defined feedback license scope.

I attached our internal annotated order form to show the change requests. Can Redwood provide an "entitlement matrix" mapping product flows (hosted API, dedicated, private) to proposed output/training rights? A simple matrix will help our procurement and security teams decide.

Also: is there precedent for a limited feedback license that allows Redwood to use anonymized usage telemetry for service improvement but not for model retraining? If you can share a short runbook or bullets we can attach to our procurement packet that would be ideal.

We'd like to keep momentum — is a 30-minute call useful this week?

Thanks,
Cassandra Liu
Senior Procurement Lead
Novum AI
attachments: Novum_Annotated_OrderForm.pdf

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>

Cassandra — thanks for the clear note and the annotated order form (received). We can absolutely produce the entitlement matrix and a short legal runbook for procurement.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- I'm attaching a first-draft "Redwood IP Entitlement Matrix" that maps Hosted / Dedicated / Private to output assignment vs license, retrain opt-in/opt-out, and telemetry/feedback scope. See attached: Redwood_IP_Entitlement_Matrix.xlsx
- I'm looping Laura (Legal) for redlines on MSA/order form language.
- Ben (Customer Success) will add practical operational notes (how opt-outs affect logs/telemetry and what we can operationally enforce).

Laura/Ben — would appreciate a quick scan for anything I missed. Cassandra — propose a 30-min sync Thursday 5/20 at 10a PT; if that works I'll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Thanks,
Priyom Das

From: laura_bennett@redwood.inference
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: Cassandra Liu <cassandra@novum.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Output entitlements & training — order form follow-up

Priyom / Ben / Cassandra — quick legal read. High level: the matrix is a good framing; below are redline asks and open questions. I attached a tracked version of the MSA redlines (Redlines_MSA_v2.docx).

Key points and suggested language approaches:
1) Output ownership:
   - For Hosted and Dedicated we should offer customers a non-exclusive, perpetual, sublicensable license to outputs for their internal business purposes; assignment is generally a blocker for hosted services.
   - For Private (on-prem/VPC) we can be more permissive: assignment or exclusive productization rights can be negotiated case-by-case (include a checkbox in the order form).
2) Training & Feedback license:
   - Propose a bifurcated approach: (a) telemetry/usage data for service improvement (aggregated/anonymized) — Redwood may use; (b) customer-provided content (prompts, files) — default to opt-out of retraining; opt-in can be provided via explicit order form selection and technical scoping.
   - Add a 30-day notice period before using any customer-provided data for model updates and require removal/certificate if requested.
3) Operational guardrails:
   - Add a definition of "anonymized" and a short list of prohibited uses (e.g., no training on verbatim PII, no re-distribution of customer outputs as a Redwood product).

Open questions for Novum:
- Would Novum accept a license (rather than assignment) for Hosted/Dedicated for outputs? If not, we should flag Private-only assignment as the fallback.
- For feedback/telemetry, do you require per-project opt-out (by route) or a global opt-out?

I kept edits conservative so we can move quickly. Happy to take the call Thursday.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
attachments: Redlines_MSA_v2.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
Cc: Cassandra Liu <cassandra@novum.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Output entitlements & training — order form follow-up

Adding a quick ops perspective. Two practical notes to include in the runbook:

1) Implementation impact of opt-outs:
   - Retrain opt-out: if Novum chooses opt-out, we will stop routing customer content into internal retraining pipelines; however, certain aggregated metrics and feature-usage telemetry (latency, token counts) will still flow into our monitoring systems — we can flag these as excluded from retraining.
   - Route-level opt-out: we can support per-route settings for Dedicated and Hosted with simple header flags; Private deployments: enforcement is customer-managed, we provide a config guide.
2) Evidence & audit:
   - For procurement, customers often request an "evidence pack" showing logs demonstrating data segregation. We can provide an ops runbook excerpt and example audit log snippet (no real logs) as an attachment.

If Novum wants assignment for Hosted, that creates operational difficulties (would likely require dedicated private tenancy and additional contractual security commitments). Recommend we propose license-for-hosted, assignment-possible-for-private.

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Mike Turner <mike.turner@novum.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>, laura_bennett@redwood.inference, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: Cassandra Liu <cassandra@novum.ai>, Novum Legal <contracts@novum.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Output entitlements & training — order form follow-up

Team — thanks for the quick responses and the matrix. A few clarifications from Novum Security/Procurement: 

- Hosted vs Private: Novum's legal team will not accept a mere license for outputs for our primary product features — assignment is their preference due to downstream regulatory obligations. That said, we can trade assignment for a narrower scope: assignment limited to "Client Productization of outputs generated solely from Client-provided prompts and files." In other words, outputs that are not mixed with public system prompts.

- Feedback license: the telemetry/service improvement carve is close. We need guarantee that any customer-provided sample used for model improvement will be stripped of identifiers and accepted only after Novum's review. Can we operationalize a "sample approval" flow?

- Evidence: procurement needs a one-page runbook describing the opt-out mechanism, who to contact for audit evidence, and estimated time to produce an audit pack.

We're okay with Private deployment being the path for assignment; but given deal timelines (we're targeting pilot in July), we need the firm language to flow into procurement this week. Can Redwood send a short, redlined paragraph we can include in our packet that states the proposed assignment carve (scoped as above) and the feedback/sample approval flow?

-Mike
Procurement Manager
Novum AI

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>
To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@novum.ai>, Cassandra Liu <cassandra@novum.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Output entitlements & training — order form follow-up

Mike / Cassandra — thanks, this is helpful and actionable. Quick summary and proposed deliverables (we will attach these to the procurement packet):

1) Short redline (1 paragraph) offering: For Hosted/Dedicated: non-exclusive perpetual license to Outputs for Customer internal business purposes; assignment only available for Private deployments or where Customer purchases dedicated private tenancy. For Private: assignment limited to outputs generated solely from Customer-provided prompts/files (no mixture with Redwood system prompts).

2) Feedback/sample approval flow (one-page runbook): Redwood will provide a sample approval process where any customer-provided sample intended for model improvement is submitted to Customer for review. Samples must be stripped of identifiers and require written approval before use in retraining. Redwood will provide a certificate of deletion/usage upon request.

3) Evidence pack summary (one page): ops runbook excerpt, example audit log stub, and contact point for audit requests (security-audit@redwood.inference). Estimated turnaround: 5 business days for a standard audit pack.

I'll get Laura to draft the single-paragraph redline and Ben to prepare the runbook stub. We can send all three artifacts by EOD tomorrow and share a one-page summary for your procurement packet.

If that works, I'll send a brief calendar invite for a 30-min alignment tomorrow to finalize wording before you circulate to Legal.

Best,
Priyom
